summary.zh: 日本关东军炸毁南满铁路柳条湖段并进攻沈阳北大营，中国抗日战争由此开始。
summary.en: The Japanese Kwantung Army blew up the South Manchuria Railway near Liutiaohu and attacked Beidaying in Shenyang, beginning China’s war of resistance.

description.zh:
1931 年 9 月 18 日夜，日本关东军自行炸毁沈阳北郊柳条湖附近的南满铁路路轨，反诬中国军队所为，随即进攻东北军北大营和沈阳城。此后数月，日军侵占东北大部。

本事件日期与地点为通行说法，具体战斗经过待史料校订。
description.en:
On the night of 18 September 1931, the Japanese Kwantung Army destroyed a section of the South Manchuria Railway near Liutiaohu, blamed Chinese troops, and attacked Beidaying and Shenyang. Within months Japanese forces occupied most of the Northeast.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts; details await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日军西进占领锦州，东北军退入关内，辽西沦陷。
summary.en: Japanese forces advanced west and took Jinzhou; the Northeast Army withdrew inside the Great Wall, leaving western Liaoning occupied.

description.zh:
九一八事变后，日军沿南满铁路向北推进，同时西进辽西。1932 年 1 月 3 日占领锦州，东北军在张学良命令下未作有力抵抗即退入关内，辽西与热河门户洞开。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
After the Mukden Incident, Japanese forces pushed north along the South Manchuria Railway and west into western Liaoning. They occupied Jinzhou on 3 January 1932; the Northeast Army, under Zhang Xueliang’s orders, withdrew inside the Great Wall without effective resistance, leaving western Liaoning and the approaches to Rehe open.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日军进攻上海闸北，第十九路军等部奋起抵抗，淞沪地区爆发激烈战斗。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Zhabei in Shanghai; the 19th Route Army and other Chinese units resisted in fierce fighting.

description.zh:
1932 年 1 月 28 日，日军以保护侨民为借口进攻上海闸北。第十九路军在蒋光鼐、蔡廷锴指挥下抵抗，双方在淞沪地区激战至 3 月。5 月，中日签订《淞沪停战协定》。

本事件日期与地点为通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 28 January 1932, Japanese forces attacked Zhabei in Shanghai under the pretext of protecting residents. The 19th Route Army, commanded by Jiang Guangnai and Cai Tingkai, resisted until March. In May, China and Japan signed the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日军占领哈尔滨，东北主要城市至此基本沦陷。
summary.en: Japanese forces captured Harbin, completing the occupation of the Northeast’s major cities.

description.zh:
1932 年 2 月 5 日，日军进入哈尔滨。此前齐齐哈尔、锦州等地已相继失守，东北三省主要城市至此基本被日军控制。

本事件为路线分段端点，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
Japanese troops entered Harbin on 5 February 1932. Qiqihar, Jinzhou, and other cities had already fallen, leaving the major cities of the three northeastern provinces largely under Japanese control.

This event marks a route segment endpoint; the date follows conventional accounts and awaits historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

place.en: Changchun, Jilin (called “Xinjing” by the puppet state)

summary.zh: 日本扶植溥仪在长春成立伪满洲国，东北被纳入日本殖民统治体系。
summary.en: Japan installed Puyi as head of the puppet state of Manchukuo in Changchun, placing the Northeast under colonial rule.

description.zh:
1932 年 3 月 1 日，日本扶植清朝末代皇帝溥仪在长春成立伪满洲国，随后以“日满议定书”等形式加以控制。中国政府与国际联盟均未承认该政权。

本事件为政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 1 March 1932, Japan installed Puyi, the last Qing emperor, as head of the puppet state of Manchukuo in Changchun, later controlling it through agreements such as the Japan-Manchukuo Protocol. Neither the Chinese government nor the League of Nations recognized the regime.

This is a political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

sources.title: 《剑桥中华民国史》
sources.author: 费正清、费维恺编
sources.note: 伪满政权建立背景参考

name.zh: 国联李顿调查团赴东北

summary.zh: 国际联盟调查团抵达东北调查九一八事变，报告否认伪满洲国合法性，但未认定日本为侵略者。
summary.en: The League of Nations commission reached the Northeast to investigate the Mukden Incident; its report denied Manchukuo’s legitimacy but stopped short of naming Japan an aggressor.

description.zh:
1932 年 4 月，国际联盟李顿调查团抵达东北，调查九一八事变后的局势。10 月公布的调查报告承认东北是中国领土、否认伪满洲国的合法性，但也未将日本定为侵略者，主张由国际共管。日本随后退出国际联盟。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In April 1932 the League of Nations Lytton Commission reached the Northeast to investigate the situation after the Mukden Incident. Its report, published in October, recognized the Northeast as Chinese territory and denied the legality of Manchukuo, but did not name Japan as an aggressor and proposed international administration. Japan subsequently withdrew from the League.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《剑桥中华民国史》
sources.author: 费正清、费维恺编
sources.note: 国联调处与李顿报告参考

name.en: Signing of the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement

summary.zh: 中日签订《淞沪停战协定》，一·二八事变结束，中国军队退出上海市区。
summary.en: China and Japan signed the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement, ending the January 28 Incident and requiring Chinese troops to withdraw from urban Shanghai.

description.zh:
1932 年 5 月 5 日，中日双方签订《淞沪停战协定》，规定上海为非武装区，中国军队不得驻守市区，日军则可留驻部分区域。一·二八事变至此结束，但协定被舆论视为屈辱让步。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 5 May 1932 China and Japan signed the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement, making Shanghai a demilitarized zone: Chinese troops were barred from the urban area while Japanese forces could remain in parts of it. The January 28 Incident thus ended, though the agreement was widely seen as a humiliating concession.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 一·二八事变后，第十九路军由上海调驻福建。
summary.en: After the January 28 Incident the 19th Route Army moved from Shanghai to Fujian.

description.zh:
1932 年 5 月《淞沪停战协定》签订后，第十九路军由上海调驻福建。1933 年 11 月，该部在福州发动福建事变，另立政府，次年失败。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
After the Shanghai Ceasefire Agreement of May 1932, the 19th Route Army moved from Shanghai to Fujian. In November 1933 it launched the Fujian Incident at Fuzhou and formed a separate government, which collapsed the following year.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

place.zh: 河北山海关（今属秦皇岛）

summary.zh: 日军进攻山海关，东北军何柱国部抵抗，榆关三日失守，长城抗战序幕拉开。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Shanhaiguan; He Zhuguo’s Northeast Army troops resisted for three days before the pass fell, opening the Great Wall campaign.

description.zh:
1933 年 1 月 1 日，日军以炮火进攻山海关，东北军第九旅何柱国部奋起抵抗。守军兵力单薄、后援不继，1 月 3 日榆关失守。此役是九一八事变后中国军队在华北的首次有组织抵抗，也被视为长城抗战的序幕。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 1 January 1933 Japanese artillery opened the attack on Shanhaiguan, and He Zhuguo’s 9th Brigade of the Northeast Army resisted. With insufficient troops and no reinforcements, the pass fell on 3 January. It was the first organized Chinese resistance in North China after the Mukden Incident and is regarded as the opening of the Great Wall campaign.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日军分路进攻热河，中国守军节节败退，承德于三月失守。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Rehe along several axes; Chinese defenders fell back and Chengde was lost in March.

description.zh:
1933 年 2 月 21 日，关东军与伪军分路向热河进攻，中国守军指挥不一、士气低落，防线迅速崩溃。3 月 4 日日军占领承德，热河全省沦陷，东北全部落入日本控制，日军兵锋直指长城各口。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 21 February 1933 the Kwantung Army and puppet troops attacked Rehe along several axes. Chinese defenders, poorly coordinated and demoralized, collapsed quickly. Chengde fell on 4 March, the whole province was occupied, and the Japanese advance reached the Great Wall passes.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日军占领承德，热河全省沦陷，东北四省全部被日本控制。
summary.en: Japanese forces occupied Chengde and the whole of Rehe, completing the occupation of the four northeastern provinces.

description.zh:
1933 年 3 月 4 日，日军先头部队进入承德，热河省主席汤玉麟此前已弃城逃走。热河沦陷后，东北四省全部被日本控制，日军与中国军队在长城一线形成对峙。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 4 March 1933 Japanese advance units entered Chengde after provincial chairman Tang Yulin had fled. With Rehe lost, all four northeastern provinces were under Japanese control, and Japanese and Chinese forces faced each other along the Great Wall.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 中国军队在喜峰口、古北口、冷口等长城关口抗击日军，最终以《塘沽协定》收场。
summary.en: Chinese troops fought Japanese forces at Xifengkou, Gubeikou, and Lengkou along the Great Wall until the Tanggu Truce ended the campaign.

description.zh:
1933 年 3 月至 5 月，中国军队依托长城各口抗击日军。喜峰口方面第二十九军以大刀夜袭闻名，古北口方面中央军第十七军等部顽强防守，冷口、界岭口亦反复争夺。由于装备与指挥劣势，中国军队最终后撤，5 月 31 日签订《塘沽协定》。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
From March to May 1933 Chinese forces defended the Great Wall passes. At Xifengkou the 29th Army became known for night raids with broadswords; at Gubeikou the Central Army’s 17th Army and others held on stubbornly; Lengkou and Jielingkou also saw repeated fighting. Hampered by inferior equipment and coordination, the Chinese forces eventually withdrew, and the Tanggu Truce was signed on 31 May.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 第二十九军在喜峰口以大刀夜袭日军，取得长城抗战中著名胜利。
summary.en: The 29th Army’s night raids with broadswords at Xifengkou produced one of the best-known victories of the Great Wall campaign.

description.zh:
1933 年 3 月 9 日，日军进攻喜峰口，第二十九军宋哲元部驰援。11 日夜，赵登禹、佟泽光等率部攀山绕袭日军营地，以大刀近战重创敌军。喜峰口战斗打破了日军不可战胜的形象，也让第二十九军声名大振。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 9 March 1933 Japanese forces attacked Xifengkou and Song Zheyuan’s 29th Army rushed to defend it. On the night of 11 March, Zhao Dengyu and Tong Zeguang led troops over the mountains to raid Japanese camps, inflicting heavy losses in close combat with broadswords. The battle shattered the image of Japanese invincibility and made the 29th Army famous.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 中央军第十七军等部在古北口、南天门一线与日军反复争夺，伤亡惨重。
summary.en: The Central Army’s 17th Army and other units fought repeated actions at Gubeikou and Nantianmen, suffering heavy casualties.

description.zh:
1933 年 3 月 10 日，日军进攻古北口，东北军与中央军第十七军等部仓促接战。此后双方在南天门一线反复争夺至 4 月下旬，中国军队伤亡惨重但仍迟滞了日军推进。古北口是长城抗战中战斗最激烈的方向之一。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 10 March 1933 Japanese forces attacked Gubeikou, where Northeast Army and Central Army units of the 17th Army engaged them. Fighting around Nantianmen continued into late April; Chinese casualties were heavy, but the defense delayed the Japanese advance. Gubeikou was one of the most bitterly contested sectors of the Great Wall campaign.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

name.zh: 察哈尔民众抗日同盟军成立
name.en: Establishment of the Chahar People’s Anti-Japanese Allied Army

summary.zh: 冯玉祥、吉鸿昌等在张家口组织抗日同盟军，北上收复多伦等失地。
summary.en: Feng Yuxiang, Ji Hongchang, and others formed the Anti-Japanese Allied Army in Zhangjiakou and moved north to recover lost territory including Duolun.

description.zh:
1933 年 5 月，冯玉祥、吉鸿昌、方振武等在张家口成立察哈尔民众抗日同盟军，号召武装抗日、收复失地。同盟军北上作战，一度收复康保、宝昌、沽源和多伦，但在日军与国民党当局的双重压力下于同年秋解散。

建制事件，不单独绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1933 Feng Yuxiang, Ji Hongchang, Fang Zhenwu, and others formed the Chahar People’s Anti-Japanese Allied Army at Zhangjiakou, calling for armed resistance and the recovery of lost territory. It advanced north and briefly retook Kangbao, Baochang, Guyuan, and Duolun, but was disbanded that autumn under pressure from both Japan and the Nationalist government.

An organizational event with no separate route; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 中日签订《塘沽协定》，中国默认日军对东北、热河的控制，冀东被划为非武装区。
summary.en: China and Japan signed the Tanggu Truce, tacitly accepting Japanese control of the Northeast and Rehe and creating a demilitarized zone in eastern Hebei.

description.zh:
1933 年 5 月 31 日，中国代表熊斌与日本代表冈村宁次在塘沽签订停战协定。协定规定中国军队撤至延庆、昌平、高丽营、顺义、通州、香河、宝坻、林亭口、宁河、芦台一线以西以南，冀东划为非武装区。中国实际上默认了日本对东北和热河的控制。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 31 May 1933 Chinese representative Xiong Bin and Japanese representative Okamura Yasuji signed a truce at Tanggu. Chinese troops were to withdraw west and south of a line through Yanqing, Changping, Gaoliying, Shunyi, Tongzhou, Xianghe, Baodi, Lintingkou, Ninghe, and Lutai, and eastern Hebei became a demilitarized zone. China thus tacitly accepted Japanese control of the Northeast and Rehe.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

place.zh: 察哈尔多伦（今属内蒙古）

summary.zh: 察哈尔抗日同盟军收复多伦，为九一八事变后中国军队首次收复失地。
summary.en: The Chahar Anti-Japanese Allied Army retook Duolun, the first recovery of lost territory by Chinese forces after the Mukden Incident.

description.zh:
1933 年 7 月，察哈尔民众抗日同盟军围攻多伦，经数日激战于 7 月 12 日收复该城。这是九一八事变后中国军队首次从日军及其伪军手中收复失地，在舆论上引起很大反响。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In July 1933 the Chahar People’s Anti-Japanese Allied Army besieged Duolun and retook the town on 12 July after several days of fighting. It was the first recovery of lost territory from Japanese and puppet forces after the Mukden Incident and caused a sensation in public opinion.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 第十九路军在福州另立政府，次年失败。
summary.en: The 19th Route Army set up a separate government at Fuzhou, which collapsed the following year.

description.zh:
1933 年 11 月 20 日，第十九路军将领蒋光鼐、蔡廷锴等在福州发动福建事变，成立“中华共和国人民革命政府”，不久在南京政府军事压力下失败。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 20 November 1933 Jiang Guangnai, Cai Tingkai, and other 19th Route Army commanders launched the Fujian Incident at Fuzhou and established the “People’s Revolutionary Government of the Chinese Republic,” which soon collapsed under military pressure from Nanjing.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

name.en: Puyi Enthroned as Emperor of Manchukuo

summary.zh: 溥仪在长春称“满洲帝国皇帝”，伪满政权进一步制度化。
summary.en: Puyi was enthroned as “Emperor of Manchukuo” in Changchun, further institutionalizing the puppet regime.

description.zh:
1934 年 3 月 1 日，溥仪在长春称“满洲帝国皇帝”，改元“康德”。伪满政权在日本关东军控制下进一步完善殖民统治机构，但始终未获中国政府与国际社会普遍承认。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 1 March 1934 Puyi was enthroned as “Emperor of Manchukuo” in Changchun and adopted the era name Kangde. Under Kwantung Army control the puppet state further developed its colonial institutions, but it was never widely recognized by the Chinese government or the international community.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 日本外务省发表天羽声明，反对列强援助中国，暴露独占中国的意图。
summary.en: Japan’s Foreign Ministry issued the Amau Statement, opposing foreign aid to China and revealing its aim of monopolizing China.

description.zh:
1934 年 4 月 17 日，日本外务省情报部长天羽英二发表非正式声明，称日本对东亚有特殊责任，反对列强向中国提供武器、借款或技术援助。声明被中国与英美等国视为“亚洲门罗主义”，加剧了华北危机前的紧张局势。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 17 April 1934 Amau Eiji, spokesman of Japan’s Foreign Ministry, issued an informal statement claiming a special Japanese responsibility in East Asia and opposing foreign arms, loans, or technical aid to China. China, Britain, and the United States saw it as an “Asian Monroe Doctrine,” heightening tensions before the North China crisis.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

summary.zh: 日本驻南京副领事藏本英明失踪，日方借机陈兵施压，数日后其被发现在紫金山隐居。
summary.en: A Japanese vice-consul in Nanjing disappeared; Japan massed warships as a pretext, but he was found days later hiding in the Zijin Mountains.

description.zh:
1934 年 6 月 9 日，日本驻南京总领事馆副领事藏本英明失踪。日本方面宣称其被中国方面绑架，调集军舰施压。6 月 13 日，藏本在南京紫金山被发现，自称因精神苦闷出走，日方的借口随之破产。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 9 June 1934 Kuramoto, a vice-consul at the Japanese consulate in Nanjing, disappeared. Japan claimed he had been kidnapped by the Chinese side and massed warships as pressure. On 13 June he was found in the Zijin Mountains outside Nanjing, saying he had left because of mental distress, and the Japanese pretext collapsed.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

name.en: Chahar East Incident and the Datan Accord

summary.zh: 日军在察东挑起冲突，迫使中国接受大滩口约，中国军队撤出察东。
summary.en: Japan provoked clashes in eastern Chahar and forced China to accept the Datan Accord, withdrawing Chinese troops from the area.

description.zh:
1935 年 1 月，日军在察哈尔东部沽源一带挑起冲突，进攻长梁、乌泥河等地。2 月，中方与日方在大滩达成口约，中国军队撤出察东，日军获得自由行动空间。此举为同年张北事件与秦土协定埋下伏笔。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In January 1935 Japanese forces provoked clashes around Guyuan in eastern Chahar, attacking Changliang, Wunihe, and other places. In February China and Japan reached an oral accord at Datan: Chinese troops withdrew from eastern Chahar and Japanese forces gained freedom of movement. The episode set the stage for the Zhangbei Incident and the Qin-Doihara Agreement later that year.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

name.en: Hebei Incident and the He-Umezu Agreement

summary.zh: 日军借河北事件施压，中国方面被迫接受撤换军政人员、撤出中央军等要求。
summary.en: Japan used the Hebei Incident to pressure China into replacing officials and withdrawing Central Army units from Hebei.

description.zh:
1935 年 5 至 6 月，日军以孙永勤部进入滦东“非武装区”和胡白被杀事件为借口，向北平军分会代委员长何应钦提出交涉。7 月 6 日，何应钦复函日本华北驻屯军司令梅津美治郎，实质上接受日方要求，中央军与国民党党部退出河北，史称“何梅协定”。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May and June 1935 Japan used the entry of Sun Yongqin’s forces into the demilitarized zone east of the Luan River and the killing of Hu Bai as pretexts to press He Yingqin, acting chairman of the Beiping Military Council. On 6 July He replied to Umezu Yoshijiro, commander of the Japanese garrison in North China, effectively accepting Japanese demands: Central Army units and Nationalist Party offices withdrew from Hebei. The exchange is known as the He-Umezu Agreement.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

name.en: Zhangbei Incident and the Qin-Doihara Agreement

summary.zh: 日军借张北事件迫使中国接受察哈尔省撤军、取缔抗日活动等条件。
summary.en: Japan used the Zhangbei Incident to force China to withdraw troops from Chahar and suppress anti-Japanese activities.

description.zh:
1935 年 6 月，日本特务在张北被中国守军盘查，日方借机提出交涉。6 月 27 日，秦德纯与土肥原贤二签订协定，中国方面同意撤换有关人员、撤退察哈尔省境内国民党军与党部，并取缔抗日活动。察哈尔主权进一步受损。

外交事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In June 1935 Japanese agents were stopped and questioned by Chinese guards at Zhangbei, and Japan used the incident to demand concessions. On 27 June Qin Dechun and Doihara Kenji signed an agreement under which China replaced the officers involved, withdrew Nationalist troops and party offices from Chahar, and suppressed anti-Japanese activities. Chahar’s sovereignty was further eroded.

A diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

name.zh: 冀东防共自治委员会成立

summary.zh: 殷汝耕在通州成立冀东防共自治委员会，冀东二十二县脱离南京管辖。
summary.en: Yin Rugeng set up the East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Council at Tongzhou, detaching 22 counties from Nanjing’s authority.

description.zh:
1935 年 11 月 25 日，殷汝耕在通州成立“冀东防共自治委员会”，宣布冀东二十二县“自治”，实际处于日本控制之下。此举是华北自治运动的高潮，直接引发一二·九运动。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 25 November 1935 Yin Rugeng established the “East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Council” at Tongzhou, declaring 22 counties of eastern Hebei “autonomous” under de facto Japanese control. It marked the peak of the North China autonomy movement and directly triggered the December Ninth Movement.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

summary.zh: 北平学生举行抗日救亡请愿游行，推动全国抗日救亡运动高涨。
summary.en: Students in Beiping marched to demand resistance and national salvation, helping to galvanize anti-Japanese sentiment nationwide.

description.zh:
1935 年 12 月 9 日，北平学生数千人举行抗日救亡请愿游行，反对华北自治，要求停止内战、一致对外。运动迅速扩展到全国，成为抗日民族统一战线形成的重要背景。

本事件为政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 9 December 1935, thousands of students in Beiping demonstrated against the autonomy movement in North China and called for an end to civil war and united resistance. The movement spread nationwide and became an important backdrop to the formation of the anti-Japanese united front.

This is a political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

summary.zh: 北平学生举行更大规模游行，抗议冀察政务委员会成立，运动扩展至全国。
summary.en: Students in Beiping held an even larger demonstration against the Hebei-Chahar Political Council, and the movement spread nationwide.

description.zh:
1935 年 12 月 16 日，北平学生万余人举行游行，抗议冀察政务委员会成立，遭到军警镇压。运动迅速扩展到天津、上海、南京、广州等地，成为全国抗日救亡运动的新高潮，也为抗日民族统一战线的形成准备了群众基础。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 16 December 1935 more than ten thousand students marched in Beiping against the Hebei-Chahar Political Council and were suppressed by police. The movement quickly spread to Tianjin, Shanghai, Nanjing, Guangzhou, and elsewhere, becoming a new high point of national salvation activity and preparing popular ground for the anti-Japanese united front.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

name.zh: 华北自治运动与冀察政务委员会成立
name.en: North China Autonomy Movement and the Hebei-Chahar Political Council

summary.zh: 日本策动华北五省“自治”，南京国民政府被迫设立半独立性质的冀察政务委员会。
summary.en: Japan promoted “autonomy” in five North China provinces, forcing Nanjing to create the semi-autonomous Hebei-Chahar Political Council.

description.zh:
1935 年秋，日本策动华北五省“自治运动”，扶植殷汝耕在通州成立“冀东防共自治委员会”。南京国民政府在日本压力下于 12 月 18 日设立冀察政务委员会，由宋哲元任委员长，华北出现半独立局面。此举直接引发了一二·九与一二·一六运动。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In autumn 1935 Japan promoted an “autonomy movement” across five North China provinces and sponsored Yin Rugeng’s “East Hebei Anti-Communist Autonomous Council” at Tongzhou. Under Japanese pressure Nanjing established the Hebei-Chahar Political Council on 18 December, chaired by Song Zheyuan, leaving North China semi-autonomous. The move directly triggered the December Ninth and December Sixteenth movements.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 陈济棠、李宗仁等以“北上抗日”为号召反蒋，事变后和平解决。
summary.en: Chen Jitang and Li Zongren moved against Chiang Kai-shek under the banner of “marching north to resist Japan”; the incident was resolved peacefully.

description.zh:
1936 年 6 月，广东陈济棠与广西李宗仁、白崇禧联合反蒋，组织“抗日救国军”北上，史称两广事变。蒋介石分化瓦解，陈济棠部将余汉谋倒戈，7 月陈济棠下野，事变和平解决，两广重归南京国民政府统辖。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In June 1936 Chen Jitang of Guangdong joined Li Zongren and Bai Chongxi of Guangxi against Chiang Kai-shek, forming a “Anti-Japanese National Salvation Army” and marching north; the episode is known as the Liangguang Incident. Chiang undermined the coalition, Chen’s subordinate Yu Hanmou defected, and Chen stepped down in July. The incident ended peacefully and the two provinces returned to Nanjing’s authority.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

name.zh: 日军策动伪蒙军进攻绥远

summary.zh: 日本关东军策动伪蒙军自商都进攻绥远，傅作义部奋起抵抗。
summary.en: The Kwantung Army directed Mengjiang forces from Shangdu against Suiyuan, where Fu Zuoyi’s troops resisted.

description.zh:
1936 年 11 月，日本关东军策动德王所属伪蒙军自商都一带西进，进攻绥远东部。绥远省主席傅作义率晋绥军迎战，先后取得红格尔图与百灵庙战斗的胜利。绥远抗战得到全国各界慰问与支援，成为西安事变前抗日情绪高涨的重要背景。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In November 1936 the Kwantung Army directed Prince De’s Mengjiang forces westward from the Shangdu area against eastern Suiyuan. Suiyuan chairman Fu Zuoyi led Shanxi-Suiyuan troops to meet them and won the battles of Honggeertu and Bailingmiao. The Suiyuan campaign drew nationwide support and helped raise anti-Japanese sentiment before the Xi’an Incident.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 傅作义部在红格尔图击退伪蒙军进攻，绥远抗战由此展开。
summary.en: Fu Zuoyi’s forces repelled the Mengjiang attack at Honggeertu, opening the Suiyuan campaign.

description.zh:
1936 年 11 月 15 日，伪蒙军在日本顾问指挥下进攻红格尔图。傅作义部骑兵与守军协同反击，经数日激战将其击退，毙伤俘敌数百人。红格尔图战斗是绥远抗战的首场胜利，为随后收复百灵庙创造了条件。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 15 November 1936 Mengjiang troops under Japanese advisers attacked Honggeertu. Fu Zuoyi’s cavalry and garrison counterattacked and, after several days of fighting, drove them back with hundreds of casualties and prisoners. The victory at Honggeertu opened the Suiyuan campaign and paved the way for the recovery of Bailingmiao.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 傅作义部奇袭百灵庙，取得绥远抗战决定性胜利，全国慰问运动高涨。
summary.en: Fu Zuoyi’s surprise attack on Bailingmiao won a decisive victory in the Suiyuan campaign and triggered nationwide support.

description.zh:
1936 年 11 月 23 日夜，傅作义部在严寒中长途奔袭百灵庙，经一夜激战于 24 日攻克该地，歼灭伪蒙军一部并缴获大量物资。百灵庙大捷震动全国，各界纷纷组织慰问与捐款，成为绥远抗战的标志性胜利。

日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On the night of 23 November 1936 Fu Zuoyi’s troops marched through severe cold to surprise Bailingmiao and, after a night of fighting, took it on 24 November, destroying part of the Mengjiang force and capturing large quantities of supplies. The victory caused a national sensation, with organizations across the country sending condolences and donations, and became the emblematic success of the Suiyuan campaign.

Dates and locations follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.title: 《日本帝国主义侵华档案资料选编》
sources.author: 中央档案馆等编

summary.zh: 沈钧儒等七位救国会领袖在上海被捕，引发全国抗议。
summary.en: Seven leaders of the National Salvation Association, including Shen Junru, were arrested in Shanghai, prompting nationwide protests.

description.zh:
1936 年 11 月 23 日，南京国民政府以“危害民国”罪名在上海逮捕沈钧儒、章乃器、邹韬奋、李公朴、沙千里、史良、王造时七位救国会领袖，史称“七君子事件”。事件激起全国各界抗议，进一步推动了抗日救亡运动。

政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 23 November 1936 the Nanjing government arrested seven leaders of the National Salvation Association in Shanghai—Shen Junru, Zhang Naiqi, Zou Taofen, Li Gongpu, Sha Qianli, Shi Liang, and Wang Zaoshi—on charges of “endangering the Republic.” Known as the Seven Gentlemen Incident, the arrests provoked nationwide protests and further strengthened the national salvation movement.

A political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

summary.zh: 张学良、杨虎城在西安扣留蒋介石，促成停止内战、联共抗日的转折。
summary.en: Zhang Xueliang and Yang Hucheng detained Chiang Kai-shek in Xi’an, leading to a turn toward ending the civil war and resisting Japan.

description.zh:
1936 年 12 月 12 日，东北军将领张学良与第十七路军将领杨虎城在西安扣留蒋介石，要求停止内战、一致抗日。经多方斡旋，事变和平解决，为抗日民族统一战线的形成创造了条件。

本事件为政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 12 December 1936, Zhang Xueliang of the Northeast Army and Yang Hucheng of the 17th Route Army detained Chiang Kai-shek in Xi’an, demanding an end to the civil war and united resistance against Japan. The incident was resolved peacefully, helping pave the way for the anti-Japanese united front.

This is a political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

name.en: The 29th Army and the defense of Lugouqiao

summary.zh: 第29军在卢沟桥奋起抵抗日军。
summary.en: The 29th Army resisted the Japanese at Lugouqiao.

description.zh: 1937 年 7 月 7 日卢沟桥事变后，第29军奋起抵抗，副军长佟麟阁、师长赵登禹在后续作战中阵亡。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: After the Lugouqiao Incident on July 7, 1937, the 29th Army resisted the Japanese; deputy commander Tong Linge and division commander Zhao Dengyu were killed in subsequent fighting. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

summary.zh: 日军在卢沟桥附近挑起冲突并进攻宛平城，中国全面抗战由此爆发。
summary.en: Japanese forces provoked a clash near the Marco Polo Bridge and attacked Wanping, marking the start of full-scale Chinese resistance.

description.zh:
1937 年 7 月 7 日夜，日军在北平西南卢沟桥附近演习，借口士兵失踪要求进入宛平城搜查，遭拒后发动进攻。中国守军第二十九军奋起抵抗，战事迅速扩大。

本事件为路线分段端点，日期与地点为通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On the night of 7 July 1937, Japanese troops on exercise near the Marco Polo Bridge demanded entry into Wanping to search for a missing soldier. After being refused, they attacked. The Chinese 29th Army resisted, and the fighting quickly escalated.

This event marks a route segment endpoint; date and location follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 日军进攻南口，平绥线作战展开。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Nankou, opening operations along the Beiping-Suiyuan railway.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月，日军进攻河北南口，平绥线作战展开。日期与经过为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: In August 1937, Japanese forces attacked Nankou, Hebei, opening operations along the Beiping-Suiyuan railway. Dates and details follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 第13军在南口抗击日军，掩护平绥线。
summary.en: The 13th Army resisted the Japanese at Nankou, covering the Beiping-Suiyuan railway.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月，第13军（军长汤恩伯）在河北南口抗击日军，掩护平绥线。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: In August 1937, the 13th Army under Tang Enbo resisted Japanese forces at Nankou, Hebei, covering the Beiping-Suiyuan railway. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

summary.zh: 中国海军在江阴段沉船封江，阻止日军溯江而上。
summary.en: The Chinese navy sank ships to block the Yangtze at Jiangyin and halt the Japanese advance upstream.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 12 日，中国海军在长江江阴段沉船封江，构筑封锁线，迟滞日军溯江进攻。舰艇数量与封锁细节为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 12, 1937, the Chinese navy sank ships to block the Yangtze at Jiangyin, constructing a blockade line to delay the Japanese advance upstream. Ship numbers and details follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

sources.title: 《中华民国史》
sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

summary.zh: 中日双方在上海投入重兵鏖战三个月，中国军队粉碎了日军速战速决的企图。
summary.en: China and Japan poured troops into three months of fighting in Shanghai, thwarting Japan’s hope for a quick victory.

description.zh:
1937 年 8 月 13 日，淞沪会战爆发。中国军队先后投入数十万兵力，与日军在上海市区及周边反复争夺。11 月，中国军队西撤，上海沦陷，但会战打破了日军“三个月灭亡中国”的计划。

本事件为路线分段端点，日期与战果表述待史料校订。
description.en:
The Battle of Shanghai began on 13 August 1937. Hundreds of thousands of Chinese troops fought Japanese forces in and around the city. In November the Chinese army withdrew west and Shanghai fell, but the battle shattered Japan’s plan to conquer China in three months.

This event marks a route segment endpoint; dates and assessments await historical review.

summary.zh: 日军进攻上海，淞沪会战爆发。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Shanghai, beginning the Battle of Shanghai.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 13 日，日军进攻上海，淞沪会战爆发。日期与经过为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 13, 1937, Japanese forces attacked Shanghai, beginning the Battle of Shanghai. Dates and details follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 第8集团军参加淞沪会战，在浦东方向作战。
summary.en: The 8th Group Army fought in the Battle of Shanghai in the Pudong sector.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月，第8集团军（总司令张发奎）参加淞沪会战，在浦东方向作战。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: In August 1937, the 8th Group Army under Zhang Fakui fought in the Battle of Shanghai in the Pudong sector. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 14 日，中国空军第四大队在浙江杭州笕桥上空迎战日军飞机，取得空战战果。大队长高志航率队参战。战果数字为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 14, 1937, the Chinese Air Force’s 4th Group engaged Japanese aircraft over Jianqiao, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, scoring a combat success. Group commander Gao Zhihang led the sortie. Casualty figures follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月，第9集团军（总司令张治中）参加淞沪会战，进攻虹口、杨树浦方向。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: In August 1937, the 9th Group Army under Zhang Zhizhong fought in the Battle of Shanghai, attacking toward Hongkou and Yangshupu. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

name.en: Establishment of the First War Zone

summary.zh: 第一战区成立，负责平汉线北段作战。
summary.en: The First War Zone was established to direct operations along the northern Jin-Pu railway.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 20 日，国民政府军事委员会划分战区，第一战区负责平汉线北段，蒋介石兼任司令长官，后由程潜接任。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 20, 1937, the National Military Council divided the front into war zones. The First War Zone was responsible for the northern section of the Beijing-Hankou railway, with Chiang Kai-shek concurrently as commander and later Cheng Qian. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 第二战区成立，负责山西、绥远方向作战。
summary.en: The Second War Zone was established for operations in Shanxi and Suiyuan.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 20 日，第二战区成立，负责山西、绥远方向，阎锡山任司令长官。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 20, 1937, the Second War Zone was established for the Shanxi and Suiyuan directions, with Yan Xishan as commander. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

description.en: On August 20, 1937, the Third War Zone was established for the Shanghai direction, with Feng Yuxiang as commander and later Gu Zhutong. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 23 日，第18军（军长罗卓英）在上海罗店与日军反复争夺。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 23, 1937, the 18th Army under Luo Zhuoying fought repeated battles with Japanese forces at Luodian, Shanghai. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 红军主力改编为国民革命军第八路军。
summary.en: The main Red Army forces were reorganized as the Eighth Route Army of the National Revolutionary Army.

description.zh: 1937 年 8 月 25 日，中共中央军委发布命令，将中国工农红军主力改编为国民革命军第八路军，朱德任总指挥，彭德怀任副总指挥。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On August 25, 1937, the Central Revolutionary Military Commission ordered the main forces of the Chinese Workers’ and Peasants’ Red Army reorganized as the Eighth Route Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Zhu De as commander and Peng Dehuai as deputy commander. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 第74军在淞沪战场以第51、第58师为基干组建，后成为正面战场主力。
summary.en: The 74th Army was formed on the Songhu battlefield around the 51st and 58th Divisions and became a mainstay of the frontal war.

description.zh:
1937 年 9 月，第74军在淞沪战场以第51师、第58师为基干组建，俞济时任军长。此后参加南京保卫战、兰封会战、万家岭战斗、上高会战、常德会战与湘西会战，被称为“抗日铁军”。

建制事件，不单独绘制路线；日期与番号沿革待史料校订。
description.en:
In September 1937 the 74th Army was formed on the Songhu battlefield around the 51st and 58th Divisions, with Yu Jishi as commander. It later fought at Nanjing, Lanfeng, Wanjialing, Shanggao, Changde, and Xiangxi, and became known as the “iron army” of the resistance.

An organizational event with no separate route; dates and order of battle await historical review.

name.en: Sichuan Troops March Out to Resist Japan

summary.zh: 川军各部自四川分批出川，开赴山西、淞沪等抗日前线。
summary.en: Sichuan units left the province in successive waves for the Shanxi and Shanghai fronts.

description.zh:
1937 年 9 月起，川军各部陆续出川抗战。第22集团军（邓锡侯、孙震部）经川陕公路北上，开赴山西第二战区；第20军（杨森部）经长江东下，开赴淞沪战场。川军装备简陋，但作战顽强，伤亡惨重。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
From September 1937 Sichuan units left the province in successive waves. The 22nd Group Army under Deng Xihou and Sun Zhen moved north via the Sichuan–Shaanxi road to the 2nd War Zone in Shanxi, while the 20th Army under Yang Sen moved east along the Yangtze to the Shanghai front. Poorly equipped but tenacious, the Sichuan troops suffered heavy casualties.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

name.en: Guangxi Troops March Out to Resist Japan

summary.zh: 桂军第21集团军自广西出发，经武汉、徐州开赴淞沪战场。
summary.en: The Guangxi 21st Group Army left Guangxi via Wuhan and Xuzhou for the Shanghai front.

description.zh:
1937 年 9 月，桂军第21集团军（廖磊部）自桂林、柳州出发，经武汉、徐州开赴淞沪，10 月参加蕴藻浜反击战。桂军作战勇猛，但在日军优势火力下伤亡惨重。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In September 1937 the Guangxi 21st Group Army under Liao Lei left Guilin and Liuzhou via Wuhan and Xuzhou for Shanghai, and in October fought in the Yunzaobang counterattack. The Guangxi troops fought bravely but suffered heavy losses under Japanese firepower.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 八路军改称国民革命军第18集团军。
summary.en: The Eighth Route Army was redesignated the 18th Group Army of the National Revolutionary Army.

description.zh: 1937 年 9 月 11 日，国民政府军事委员会将八路军改称国民革命军第18集团军，朱德任总司令，彭德怀任副总司令。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On September 11, 1937, the National Military Council redesignated the Eighth Route Army as the 18th Group Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Zhu De as commander-in-chief and Peng Dehuai as deputy commander-in-chief. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 日军关东军察哈尔派遣兵团占领大同，随后沿同蒲路南下。
summary.en: The Japanese Kwantung Army’s Chahar expeditionary force took Datong and moved south along the Tongpu railway.

description.zh: 1937 年 9 月 13 日日军关东军察哈尔派遣兵团占领大同，晋北门户洞开；日军随后沿同蒲路南下，10 月 13 日猛攻忻口。
description.en: On 13 September 1937 the Kwantung Army’s Chahar force took Datong, opening northern Shanxi; the Japanese then moved south along the Tongpu railway and attacked Xinkou on 13 October.

summary.en: The Japanese 5th Division took Lingqiu and moved south against Pingxingguan.

description.en: On 20 September 1937 the Japanese 5th Division took Lingqiu county town and moved south along the Lingqiu–Pingxingguan road; on 25 September the 115th Division ambushed its supply column at Qiaogou.

summary.zh: 八路军第一一五师在平型关伏击日军，取得全面抗战初期的重要胜利。
summary.en: The 115th Division of the Eighth Route Army ambushed Japanese troops at Pingxingguan, winning an important early victory.

description.zh:
1937 年 9 月 25 日，八路军第一一五师在山西灵丘平型关东北的乔沟一带伏击日军第五师团第二十一旅团一部及辎重部队，歼敌数百人，击毁汽车、马车多辆。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 25 September 1937, the 115th Division of the Eighth Route Army ambushed part of the Japanese 5th Division’s 21st Brigade and its supply column near Qiaogou, northeast of Pingxingguan in Lingqiu, Shanxi, killing several hundred Japanese troops and destroying vehicles and wagons.

Date, location, and casualties follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

sources.author: 军事科学院军事历史研究部

name.zh: 川军第22集团军参加娘子关战斗

summary.zh: 川军第22集团军自四川北上，在娘子关一线参加保卫战。
summary.en: The Sichuan 22nd Group Army marched north and fought in the defense of Niangziguan.

description.zh:
1937 年 10 月，川军第22集团军经宝鸡、西安北上，在娘子关一线参加对日作战。川军装备低劣、补给困难，仍以重大伤亡迟滞日军。此后该部转赴山东，参加滕县保卫战。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In October 1937 the Sichuan 22nd Group Army moved north via Baoji and Xi’an and fought the Japanese at Niangziguan. Poorly equipped and badly supplied, it still delayed the Japanese at great cost. The army then moved to Shandong and fought in the defense of Tengxian.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

name.en: Establishment of the New Fourth Army

summary.zh: 南方八省红军游击队改编为国民革命军陆军新编第四军。
summary.en: Red Army guerrillas from eight southern provinces were reorganized as the New Fourth Army.

description.zh: 1937 年 10 月 12 日，国民政府军事委员会宣布将南方八省红军游击队改编为国民革命军陆军新编第四军，叶挺任军长，项英任副军长。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On October 12, 1937, the National Military Council announced the reorganization of Red Army guerrillas from eight southern provinces as the New Fourth Army of the National Revolutionary Army, with Ye Ting as commander and Xiang Ying as deputy commander. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.en: The Sichuan 20th Army moved east along the Yangtze to Shanghai and fought at Dachang and Yunzaobang.

description.zh:
1937 年 10 月，川军第20军（杨森部）经重庆、宜昌、武汉东下抵达淞沪，参加大场、蕴藻浜一带战斗。该军装备简陋，在日军火力下伤亡很大。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In October 1937 the Sichuan 20th Army under Yang Sen moved east via Chongqing, Yichang, and Wuhan to Shanghai and fought around Dachang and Yunzaobang. Poorly equipped, it suffered heavy casualties under Japanese fire.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 日军进攻忻口，忻口会战展开。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Xinkou, opening the Battle of Xinkou.

description.zh: 1937 年 10 月 13 日，日军进攻山西忻口，忻口会战展开。日期与经过为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On October 13, 1937, Japanese forces attacked Xinkou, Shanxi, opening the Battle of Xinkou. Dates and details follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

description.zh: 1937 年 10 月，第14集团军（总司令卫立煌）参加忻口会战，在山西忻口一线抗击日军。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: In October 1937, the 14th Group Army under Wei Lihuang fought in the Battle of Xinkou, resisting Japanese forces along the Xinkou line in Shanxi. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

sources.author: 中国社会科学院近代史研究所

summary.zh: 中国军队在忻口阻击日军，激战近一个月，忻口最终失守，太原随后沦陷。
summary.en: Chinese forces blocked the Japanese at Xinkou for nearly a month before the position fell and Taiyuan was lost.

description.zh:
1937 年 10 月，日军第五师团等部沿同蒲铁路南下，进攻忻口。中国第二战区部队在卫立煌指挥下依托阵地顽强抵抗，双方在忻口一线激战。日军久攻不下，后因娘子关失守、中国军队侧后受威胁，中国军队于 11 月 2 日撤退，太原于 11 月 8 日失守。此役是太原会战的重要组成部分。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In October 1937, Japanese forces including the 5th Division advanced south along the Datong–Pukou railway and attacked Xinkou. Chinese troops of the Second War Zone, commanded by Wei Lihuang, resisted stubbornly from prepared positions in fierce fighting around Xinkou. Unable to break through quickly, the Japanese exploited the fall of Niangziguan and threatened the Chinese flank and rear; Chinese forces withdrew on 2 November, and Taiyuan fell on 8 November. The battle was an important part of the Taiyuan campaign.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: The Guangxi 21st Group Army and other units counterattacked along Yunzaobang at heavy cost.

description.zh:
1937 年 10 月中下旬，中国军队在蕴藻浜一线反击日军，桂军第21集团军等部投入战斗。由于日军火力占优，反击未能奏效，桂军伤亡惨重。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In mid-to-late October 1937 Chinese forces counterattacked along Yunzaobang, with the Guangxi 21st Group Army and others committed. Japanese firepower prevailed, the counterattack failed, and the Guangxi troops suffered heavy casualties.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

description.en: In November 1937, the 10th Group Army under Liu Jianxu fought in the later stage of the Battle of Shanghai. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.en: The Jin-Cha-Ji Military Region was established at Fuping, opening a base area behind Japanese lines in North China.

description.zh: 1937 年 11 月 7 日，晋察冀军区在河北阜平成立，聂荣臻任司令员兼政治委员，开辟华北第一个敌后抗日根据地。日期与主官为通行说法，待页码级核对。
description.en: On November 7, 1937, the Jin-Cha-Ji Military Region was established at Fuping, Hebei, with Nie Rongzhen as commander and political commissar, opening North China’s first anti-Japanese base area behind enemy lines. Dates and appointments follow conventional accounts and await page-level verification.

summary.zh: 日军攻占南京后对平民和战俘实施大规模屠杀、强奸与劫掠，造成惨重伤亡。
summary.en: After capturing Nanjing, Japanese forces carried out mass killings, rape, and looting against civilians and prisoners of war.

description.zh:
1937 年 12 月 13 日，日军攻占南京。随后数周内，日军在南京及周边地区对放下武器的中国军人和无辜平民实施大规模屠杀、强奸、纵火与抢劫。远东国际军事法庭认定伤亡规模巨大。

本事件为路线分段端点，具体伤亡数字存在不同统计口径，待史料校订。
description.en:
Japanese forces captured Nanjing on 13 December 1937. In the following weeks they carried out mass killings, rape, arson, and looting against disarmed Chinese soldiers and civilians in and around the city. The International Military Tribunal for the Far East found the scale of the atrocities to be enormous.

This event marks a route segment endpoint; casualty figures vary among accounts and await historical review.

description.en: On 10 January 1938 Japanese marines landed at Qingdao, the Chinese garrison having withdrawn; the Japanese then moved west along the Jiaoji railway in preparation for the attacks on Linyi and Xuzhou.

1938 年 3 月，川军第22集团军第41军王铭章部在滕县死守，与日军第10师团激战。滕县于 3 月 17 日陷落，王铭章殉国，但川军的抵抗为台儿庄会战争取了部署时间。

In March 1938 the 41st Army of the Sichuan 22nd Group Army, under Wang Mingzhang, held Tengxian against the Japanese 10th Division. The town fell on 17 March and Wang was killed, but the resistance bought time for the Chinese deployment at Taierzhuang.

summary.en: Chinese forces inflicted a major defeat on Japanese troops at Taierzhuang, a significant victory on the frontal battlefield.

description.zh:
1938 年 3 月至 4 月，中国军队在第五战区司令长官李宗仁指挥下，于山东台儿庄地区与日军第十师团等部激战，最终取得台儿庄大捷。此役是徐州会战的重要组成部分。

description.en:
From March to April 1938, Chinese forces under Li Zongren, commander of the Fifth War Zone, fought Japanese units including the 10th Division at Taierzhuang in Shandong, winning a major victory. The battle was an important part of the Xuzhou campaign.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

description.zh:
1938 年 4 月，滇军第60军抵达徐州后投入禹王山战斗，与日军第5、第10师团激战近一个月，伤亡惨重但守住了阵地，为徐州会战主力转移争取了时间。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In April 1938 the Yunnan 60th Army reached Xuzhou and fought at Yuwangshan against the Japanese 5th and 10th Divisions for nearly a month. Though badly mauled, it held its positions and bought time for the main forces to withdraw from the Xuzhou campaign.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.en: The Japanese 14th Division crossed the Yellow River and took Heze.

description.zh: 1938 年 5 月，日军第 14 师团（土肥原贤二）自濮阳渡黄河南下，5 月 14 日占领菏泽，随后向兰封、开封推进，引发兰封会战。
description.en: In May 1938 the Japanese 14th Division under Tsuchihashi (Dohihara’s 14th) crossed the Yellow River at Puyang and took Heze on 14 May, then pushed towards Lanfeng and Kaifeng, bringing on the Lanfeng battle.

sources.title: 中国事变陆军作战史
sources.author: 日本防卫厅防卫研修所战史室
sources.note: 第 14 师团渡河与菏泽战斗

summary.zh: 中国军队围攻兰封日军第 14 师团，因日军增援与协同问题未能全歼，最终撤退。
summary.en: Chinese forces besieged the Japanese 14th Division at Lanfeng; Japanese reinforcements and coordination problems prevented a full encirclement, and the Chinese withdrew.

description.zh:
1938 年 5 月，徐州会战后期，中国军队在兰封地区围攻日军第 14 师团。中国军队一度收复兰封，但日军增援逼近，中国军队侧背受威胁，被迫撤退。此役是徐州会战的重要组成部分，也暴露了指挥协同与装备差距。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1938, late in the Xuzhou campaign, Chinese forces besieged the Japanese 14th Division around Lanfeng. Chinese troops briefly recovered Lanfeng, but as Japanese reinforcements approached and threatened their flank and rear, they were forced to withdraw. The battle was an important part of the Xuzhou campaign and exposed gaps in command coordination and equipment.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: The Yunnan 58th Army was formed with Sun Du as commander and soon moved to northern Jiangxi.

description.zh:
1938 年 6 月，为加强武汉会战兵力，滇军以 6 个团及常备训练团队在云南编成第58军，孙渡任军长。该军随后开赴赣北，隶属第9战区，参加南昌会战、长沙会战等。

description.en:
In June 1938, to strengthen the forces for the Battle of Wuhan, the Yunnan military formed the 58th Army in Yunnan from six regiments and a standing training unit, with Sun Du as commander. It then moved to northern Jiangxi under the 9th War Zone and fought in the Nanchang and Changsha campaigns.

An organizational event with no separate route; dates and order of battle await historical review.

description.en: In the later phase of the Lanfeng battle the Chinese army failed to destroy Dohihara’s 14th Division; Japanese reinforcements arrived and took Kaifeng on 6 June, the Chinese withdrawing east of Zhengzhou before the Huayuankou breach.

In September 1938 the 58th Army moved from Yunnan via Guiyang and Changsha to northern Jiangxi under the 9th War Zone. It then fought for years in northern Jiangxi and northern Hunan, taking part in the Nanchang and Changsha campaigns and guerrilla operations.

1938 年 9 至 10 月，武汉会战期间，第74军等部在江西德安万家岭地区包围日军第106师团，经激战重创该部。万家岭大捷是武汉会战中的重要胜利，也使第74军声名大振。

In September and October 1938, during the Battle of Wuhan, the 74th Army and other units encircled and mauled the Japanese 106th Division at Wanjialing in De’an, Jiangxi. The victory was an important success in the Wuhan campaign and made the 74th Army famous.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 中国第一支机械化军在广西全州整编成军，杜聿明任军长。
summary.en: China’s first mechanized army was assembled at Quanzhou, Guangxi, with Du Yuming as commander.

description.zh:
1938 年 10 月，第5军在广西全州整编成军，辖第200师、新编第22师、荣誉第1师，杜聿明任军长，是中国第一支机械化部队。1939 年参加桂南会战、主攻昆仑关；1942 年作为远征军先头部队入缅。

建制事件，不单独绘制路线；日期与番号沿革待史料校订。
description.en:
In October 1938 the 5th Army was assembled at Quanzhou, Guangxi, with the 200th Division, New 22nd Division, and Honorary 1st Division under Du Yuming. It was China’s first mechanized army. In 1939 it fought in the Guangxi campaign and led the attack on Kunlun Pass; in 1942 it entered Burma as the spearhead of the Chinese Expeditionary Force.

An organizational event with no separate route; dates and order of battle await historical review.

In October 1938 the Yunnan 184th and New 12th Divisions formed the New 3rd Army at Changsha under the 30th Army Corps. It suffered a defeat at Chongyang in Hubei in November and then fought in northern Jiangxi and northern Hunan under the 9th War Zone.

An organizational event with no separate route; dates and order of battle await historical review.

In October 1938, Japanese forces landed at Daya Bay in Guangdong and advanced along roads toward Guangzhou. The city fell on 21 October, placing an important southern port and external supply route under Japanese control.

summary.en: After the Battle of Wuhan, Japanese forces captured the city, and the war entered a phase of strategic stalemate.

description.zh:

description.en:
From June 1938, Japanese forces advanced on Wuhan from both sides of the Yangtze. Chinese troops fought the Battle of Wuhan for months before withdrawing in October. Wuhan fell on 25 October; government organs had already moved to Chongqing, and the war gradually entered a phase of strategic stalemate.

This event is linked to route segments; dates and wording await historical review.

description.zh:
1939 年 5 月，日军第 11 军向随县、枣阳地区进攻，企图打击中国第五战区主力。中国军队依托地形逐次抵抗，并在日军补给困难时反击，至 5 月下旬恢复原阵地。此役是抗战进入相持阶段后的重要作战。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1939, the Japanese 11th Army attacked the Suixian and Zaoyang areas, seeking to strike the main forces of China’s Fifth War Zone. Chinese troops used the terrain to resist in stages and counterattacked as Japanese supply lines became strained, restoring the original line by late May. It was an important operation after the war entered the stalemate phase.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

description.en:
On 14 September 1939, Japanese forces launched an offensive across the Xinqiang River in Hunan in an attempt to take Changsha. Chinese troops of the Ninth War Zone resisted in stages, drew the Japanese forward, then struck their flanks and counterattacked, forcing a withdrawal to the original line in early October. It was an important defensive battle on China’s frontal battlefield during the stalemate phase.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

In December 1939, Chinese forces launched a counteroffensive to recover Nanning and retake Kunlun Pass. The Chinese 5th Army and other units fought fierce, seesaw battles against the Japanese at the pass, finally recapturing it in January 1940 and killing the Japanese brigade commander Nakamura Masao. It was an important Chinese offensive victory in the middle years of the war.

summary.zh: 日军进攻枣阳、宜昌地区，中国军队顽强抵抗，张自忠殉国，宜昌最终失守。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked the Zaoyang and Yichang areas; Chinese troops resisted stubbornly, Zhang Zizhong was killed, and Yichang eventually fell.

description.zh:
1940 年 5 月，日军第十一军向枣阳、襄阳、宜昌地区发动进攻，企图歼灭中国第五战区主力并控制长江上游门户。中国军队在枣阳、襄阳一线抵抗，第 33 集团军总司令张自忠在宜城南瓜店战斗中殉国。6 月，宜昌失守。此役中国军队伤亡重大，但保持了战区主力。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1940, the Japanese 11th Army attacked the Zaoyang, Xiangyang, and Yichang areas, seeking to destroy the main forces of China’s Fifth War Zone and control the upper Yangtze gateway. Chinese troops resisted along the Zaoyang–Xiangyang line, and Zhang Zizhong, commander of the 33rd Army Group, was killed in action near Nanguadian in Yicheng. Yichang fell in June. Chinese forces suffered heavy casualties but preserved the bulk of the war zone’s strength.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: General Zhang Zizhong, commander of the 33rd Group Army, died at Nanguadian during the Zaoyang–Yichang campaign.

description.zh:
1940 年 5 月，枣宜会战期间，第33集团军总司令张自忠率部渡襄河督战，5 月 16 日在宜城南瓜店被日军包围，力战殉国，是抗战中阵亡的最高级别中国将领之一。

人物事件，随第33集团军路线标注；日期与地点待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1940, during the Zaoyang–Yichang campaign, General Zhang Zizhong, commander of the 33rd Group Army, crossed the Xiang River to direct operations. On 16 May he was surrounded by Japanese forces at Nanguadian in Yicheng and died fighting, one of the most senior Chinese commanders killed in the war.

A biographical event marked with the 33rd Group Army route; dates and location await historical review.

place.en: Along the Zhengding–Taiyuan railway in North China (Yangquan area)

summary.zh: 八路军在华北发动大规模破袭战，打击日军交通线与据点。
summary.en: The Eighth Route Army launched a large-scale sabotage campaign against Japanese transport lines and strongpoints in North China.

description.zh:
1940 年 8 月 20 日起，八路军在华北发动以破袭正太铁路为重点的大规模进攻，先后参战部队达一百余个团。战役持续至 1941 年初，对日军交通线和据点造成较大打击，也引起日军对华北敌后根据地的更残酷“扫荡”。

本事件日期、地点与规模表述待史料校订。
description.en:
Beginning on 20 August 1940, the Eighth Route Army launched a large offensive in North China centered on sabotaging the Zhengding–Taiyuan railway, with more than a hundred regiments eventually taking part. The campaign lasted into early 1941, damaging Japanese transport lines and strongpoints and prompting harsher Japanese “mopping-up” operations against base areas.

Dates, location, and scale await historical review.

description.en: On the night of 20 August 1940 the Hundred Regiments Offensive opened; the 129th Division broke the western Zhengding–Taiyuan railway, taking posts between Yangquan and Shouyang, destroying track and bridges, with fighting extending to the approaches of Yuci.

1940 年 9 月，日军入侵越南北部，威胁滇南。第60军第182、184师由赣北靖安、安义一线调回云南，防守滇越边境。此后第60军长期驻守滇南，直至抗战胜利。

description.en:
In September 1940 Japan moved into northern Vietnam and threatened southern Yunnan. The 60th Army’s 182nd and 184th Divisions were transferred from Jing’an and Anyi in northern Jiangxi back to Yunnan to guard the Sino-Vietnamese border. The army then held southern Yunnan until the end of the war.

description.en:
From October 1940 the 60th Army held the Mengzi–Hekou line, using the Yunnan–Vietnam railway and the Red River defenses to block a Japanese advance from Vietnam into Yunnan. The defense of southern Yunnan lasted five years until the Japanese surrender in 1945.

summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Shanggao; Chinese troops encircled and counterattacked, winning a major victory.

description.zh:
1941 年 3 月，日军第十一军向江西上高地区进攻，企图打击中国第九战区部队。中国军队依托地形逐次抵抗，诱敌深入后实施包围反击，至 4 月上旬收复失地，取得上高会战胜利。此役是抗战中期正面战场的一次重要胜利。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In March 1941, the Japanese 11th Army attacked the Shanggao area of Jiangxi, seeking to strike Chinese forces of the Ninth War Zone. Chinese troops resisted in stages using the terrain, drew the Japanese in, then counterattacked and encircled them, recovering the lost ground by early April and winning the Battle of Shanggao. It was an important victory on China’s frontal battlefield in the middle years of the war.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.zh: 日军围攻中条山中国守军，中国军队遭受重大损失，被迫南渡黄河突围。
summary.en: Japanese forces besieged Chinese troops in the Zhongtiao Mountains; the Chinese army suffered heavy losses and was forced to break out south across the Yellow River.

description.zh:
1941 年 5 月，日军集中兵力围攻山西南部中条山地区的中国军队。中国守军补给困难、指挥协同不足，在日军多路进攻下遭受重大损失，部分部队南渡黄河突围。此役是抗战中期中国正面战场的一次严重失利。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1941, Japanese forces concentrated their strength to besiege Chinese troops in the Zhongtiao Mountains of southern Shanxi. Hampered by supply difficulties and poor coordination, the Chinese defenders suffered heavy losses under multiple Japanese attacks, and part of the force broke out south across the Yellow River. It was a serious setback for China’s frontal battlefield in the middle years of the war.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: Japanese forces again attacked Changsha; Chinese troops resisted in stages and counterattacked, forcing a Japanese withdrawal to the original line in early October.

description.zh:
1941 年 9 月，日军第十一军向新墙河、汨罗江一线发起进攻，企图击破中国第九战区主力并攻取长沙。中国军队逐次抵抗，双方在长沙外围激战；日军因补给困难和中国军队侧击，于 10 月上旬退回原阵地。此役双方均有较大伤亡。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In September 1941, the Japanese 11th Army attacked across the Xinqiang and Miluo rivers, aiming to destroy the main forces of China’s Ninth War Zone and take Changsha. Chinese troops resisted in stages and fought fierce actions on the city’s outskirts. Hampered by supply difficulties and Chinese flank attacks, the Japanese withdrew to their original line in early October. Both sides suffered considerable casualties.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

This is an international event with no route drawn; the date follows Hawaii time and awaits historical review.

summary.zh: 日军第三次进攻长沙，中国军队以“天炉战法”诱敌深入并反击，取得长沙大捷。
summary.en: Japan attacked Changsha for the third time; Chinese forces drew the Japanese in and counterattacked, winning a major victory.

description.zh:
1941 年 12 月 24 日，日军第十一军再次向长沙进攻。中国第九战区司令长官薛岳采取“天炉战法”，以一部兵力逐次抵抗、诱敌深入，主力从外围侧击、合围。日军攻入长沙外围后补给困难，被迫撤退；中国军队追击，至 1942 年 1 月中旬恢复原阵地。此役是太平洋战争爆发后中国正面战场的一次重要胜利。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 24 December 1941, the Japanese 11th Army attacked Changsha again. Xue Yue, commander of China’s Ninth War Zone, employed the “heavenly furnace” tactic: a covering force resisted in stages and drew the Japanese inward while the main force struck the flanks and closed the ring. After reaching the outskirts of Changsha, the Japanese faced supply difficulties and were forced to retreat. Chinese forces pursued and restored the original line by mid-January 1942. It was an important victory on China’s frontal battlefield after the outbreak of the Pacific War.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

In early 1942, to defend the Burma Road and support the Allies, the Chinese Expeditionary Force entered Burma from Yunnan and fought alongside British troops. It engaged Japanese forces in northern and central Burma before withdrawing under unfavorable conditions.

The date is an illustrative point in February 1942; the exact entry dates await historical review.

summary.en: After the Burma defeat the 200th Division returned to western Yunnan while the New 22nd Division withdrew to India.

description.zh:
1942 年 5 月缅甸战局逆转，第5军被迫撤退。第200师经缅北退回云南保山一带，新编第22师随杜聿明部退往印度。撤退途中损失惨重。

description.en:
In May 1942 the Burma front collapsed and the 5th Army was forced to retreat. The 200th Division returned to the Baoshan area of Yunnan, while the New 22nd Division withdrew to India with Du Yuming’s headquarters. Losses during the retreat were severe.

Illustrative simplified route showing only the 200th Division’s return; the New 22nd Division’s withdrawal to India is covered by the Allied layer. Dates await historical review.

summary.zh: 缅甸战局失利后，中国远征军部分部队撤往印度，后整编为中国驻印军。
summary.en: After setbacks in Burma, part of the Chinese Expeditionary Force withdrew to India and was later reorganized as the Chinese Army in India.

description.zh:
1942 年 5 月前后，缅甸战局恶化，中国远征军部分部队经野人山等路线撤往印度，损失惨重；另一部分退回云南。撤至印度的部队后来在兰姆伽整训，整编为中国驻印军。

本事件日期为示意时间点，撤退路线与时间待史料校订。
description.en:
Around May 1942, as the situation in Burma deteriorated, part of the Chinese Expeditionary Force withdrew to India through difficult routes including the Naga Hills, suffering heavy losses; another part returned to Yunnan. The troops in India were later reorganized and trained at Ramgarh as the Chinese Army in India.

The date is an illustrative point; retreat routes and timing await historical review.

summary.en: Japanese forces attacked western Hubei; Chinese troops stubbornly defended the Shipai fortress area and thwarted the offensive.

description.zh:
1943 年 5 月，日军第十一军向鄂西地区进攻，企图夺取石牌要塞、威胁重庆。中国第六战区部队依托长江三峡地形顽强抵抗，在石牌一带与日军激战，最终迫使日军撤退。此役是抗战后期正面战场的一次重要防御胜利。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1943, the Japanese 11th Army attacked western Hubei, seeking to seize the Shipai fortress and threaten Chongqing. Chinese troops of the Sixth War Zone used the terrain of the Three Gorges to resist stubbornly, fighting fierce actions around Shipai and eventually forcing the Japanese to withdraw. It was an important defensive victory on China’s frontal battlefield in the later war years.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: The 74th Army moved from the Changsha area to Changde and fought in the Battle of Changde.

description.zh:
1943 年秋，第74军由长沙方向调防常德，第57师守常德城，军主力在外围策应。11 月常德会战爆发，第57师苦守孤城，第74军等部在外围反攻。

description.en:
In autumn 1943 the 74th Army moved from the Changsha area to Changde; the 57th Division held the city while the main force operated on the outskirts. When the Battle of Changde began in November, the 57th Division held out in the isolated city and the 74th Army counterattacked from outside.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 日军进攻常德，中国守军坚守多日后突围，中国军队随后反攻收复常德。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked Changde; the Chinese garrison held out for days before breaking out, and Chinese troops counterattacked to recover the city.

description.zh:
1943 年 11 月，日军第十一军向常德地区发起进攻，企图牵制中国军队并夺取洞庭湖周边粮区。中国第 74 军第 57 师坚守常德城，与日军激战多日，伤亡惨重后突围。中国军队外围部队随即反攻，12 月收复常德。此役战斗激烈，双方均有重大伤亡。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In November 1943, the Japanese 11th Army attacked the Changde area, seeking to pin down Chinese forces and seize the rice-producing region around Dongting Lake. The 57th Division of the Chinese 74th Army defended Changde in bitter fighting for many days before breaking out with heavy losses. Chinese forces on the periphery counterattacked and recovered the city in December. Both sides suffered major casualties.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: Leaders of China, the United States, and Britain met in Cairo and issued the Cairo Declaration, affirming the return of Chinese territories after the war.

description.zh:
1943 年 11 月 22 日至 26 日，蒋介石、罗斯福、丘吉尔在开罗举行会议，讨论对日作战与战后安排。会议发表的《开罗宣言》明确表示，日本所窃取于中国的领土，如东北、台湾、澎湖列岛等，应归还中国。

description.en:
From 22 to 26 November 1943, Chiang Kai-shek, Franklin D. Roosevelt, and Winston Churchill met in Cairo to discuss the war against Japan and postwar arrangements. The Cairo Declaration stated that territories Japan had seized from China, including the Northeast, Taiwan, and the Penghu Islands, should be returned to China.

This is a diplomatic event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

On 17 April 1944, Japan launched Operation Ichi-Go, attacking across Henan, Hunan, and Guangxi. description.en:
In May 1944, the Chinese Expeditionary Force crossed the Salween and launched a counteroffensive against Japanese forces at Tengchong, Longling, Songshan, and other points. Working with Allied forces, Chinese troops fought fierce battles at Songshan, Tengchong, and Longling, recovered Wanding in January 1945, and opened the Ledo Road. The campaign was an important Chinese counteroffensive in western Yunnan in the later war years, coordinated with the northern Burma offensive.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

summary.en: The Chinese 10th Army held Hengyang for 47 days, inflicting heavy losses on Japanese forces before the city fell.

description.zh:
1944 年 6 月，日军在豫湘桂战役中进攻衡阳。中国第 10 军约一万七千人坚守衡阳，面对优势日军的围攻，苦战 47 天，伤亡惨重，弹尽援绝，衡阳于 8 月 8 日失守。此役迟滞了日军南进，是抗战后期著名的城市防御战。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为城防示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In June 1944, Japanese forces attacked Hengyang during Operation Ichi-Go. The Chinese 10th Army, about 17,000 strong, defended the city against a numerically superior Japanese siege for 47 days. With heavy casualties, ammunition exhausted, and no relief in sight, Hengyang fell on 8 August. The defense delayed the Japanese advance south and became one of the best-known urban defense battles of the later war years.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a sketch of the city defense and awaits historical review.

In spring 1945 the 18th Army assembled at Yuanling and Chenxi in western Hunan as the 4th Front Army’s mobile corps. When the Western Hunan campaign began in April, it stood ready to reinforce the Xuefeng Mountains sector.

summary.en: Allied and Chinese forces recaptured Mandalay, a major advance in the northern Burma counteroffensive.

description.en:
In March 1945, Allied and Chinese forces in the northern Burma counteroffensive reached the Mandalay area and recaptured the city on 20 March. Allied forces continued southward, and the situation in Burma became increasingly clear.

summary.zh: 日军进攻湘西芷江机场，中国军队反击，取得湘西会战胜利。
summary.en: Japanese forces attacked the Zhijiang airfield in western Hunan; Chinese troops counterattacked and won the Battle of West Hunan.

description.zh:
1945 年 4 月，日军发动湘西会战，企图破坏芷江空军基地。中国军队依托雪峰山地形顽强抵抗并反击，至 6 月收复失地，日军伤亡惨重。此役是抗战后期正面战场的一次重要胜利，也是日本投降前中国军队的最后一次大规模攻势防御作战。

本事件日期、地点与战果为通行说法，路线为战役示意，待史料校订。
description.en:
In April 1945, Japanese forces launched the Battle of West Hunan in an attempt to destroy the Zhijiang air base. Chinese troops used the terrain of the Xuefeng Mountains to resist stubbornly and counterattack, recovering the lost ground by June and inflicting heavy casualties on the Japanese. It was an important victory on China’s frontal battlefield in the final year of the war and one of the Chinese army’s last large-scale defensive-offensive operations before Japan’s surrender.

Dates, location, and assessments follow conventional accounts; the route is a campaign sketch and awaits historical review.

description.zh: 1945 年 4 月 9 日日军第 20 军自邵阳、东安出动，进攻芷江机场，湘西会战爆发；中国军队在雪峰山一线阻击并反攻，6 月日军退回原防。邵阳自 1944 年 9 月即为日军占领。
description.en: On 9 April 1945 the Japanese 20th Army moved from Shaoyang and Dong’an against the Zhijiang airfield, opening the western Hunan battle; the Chinese army held and counter-attacked along the Xuefeng mountains, and the Japanese withdrew in June. Shaoyang had been occupied since September 1944.

summary.en: Chinese forces counterattacked in Guangxi, recovering Guilin, Liuzhou, and Nanning.

description.zh:
1945 年 5 月起，中国军队在广西发起局部反攻，逐步收复豫湘桂战役中失守的城镇。随着日本宣布投降，桂柳、南宁等地相继光复。

本事件日期为示意时间点，具体作战进程待史料校订。
description.en:
From May 1945, Chinese forces launched a limited counteroffensive in Guangxi, gradually recovering towns lost during Operation Ichi-Go. With Japan’s announcement of surrender, Guilin, Liuzhou, Nanning, and other places were recovered.

The date is an illustrative point; operational details await historical review.

summary.en: 4th War Zone troops counterattacked from the Guilin direction and recovered Liuzhou and Guilin.

description.zh:
1945 年 5 月，第4战区部队在桂北发起反攻，先后收复柳州、桂林，将日军逐出广西。此役与湘西会战、滇西反攻同为抗战末期中国军队的局部反攻。

路线为示意简化，日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1945 4th War Zone troops launched a counteroffensive in northern Guangxi, recovering Liuzhou and Guilin and driving the Japanese out of the province. Together with the Western Hunan campaign and the western Yunnan counteroffensive, it was one of the limited Chinese counteroffensives at the end of the war.

Illustrative simplified route; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 新6军自云南空运芷江，担任湘西会战总预备队。
summary.en: The New 6th Army was airlifted from Yunnan to Zhijiang as the general reserve for the Western Hunan campaign.

description.zh:
1945 年 5 月，新6军（廖耀湘部）近三万人自云南昆明空运湖南芷江，担任湘西会战总预备队并担负芷江机场守备。此时战局已趋稳定，新6军未及全面参战。

空运航线为示意直线，非地面行军；日期取通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
In May 1945 nearly 30,000 troops of the New 6th Army under Liao Yaoxiang were airlifted from Kunming, Yunnan, to Zhijiang, Hunan, as the general reserve for the Western Hunan campaign and to guard Zhijiang airfield. By then the situation had stabilized and the army did not enter combat in full.

Shown as a schematic air bridge, not a ground march; dates follow conventional accounts and await historical review.

summary.zh: 美国在广岛投下原子弹，加速了日本投降的进程。
summary.en: The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, accelerating Japan’s surrender.

description.zh:
1945 年 8 月 6 日，美国在日本广岛投下原子弹，造成大量人员伤亡。8 月 9 日，美国又在长崎投下原子弹。核打击与苏联出兵东北共同加速了日本投降。

本事件为国际事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 6 August 1945, the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, causing massive casualties. On 9 August, another bomb was dropped on Nagasaki. The nuclear strikes, together with the Soviet entry into the war in the Northeast, accelerated Japan’s surrender.

This is an international event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

name.en: Soviet Declaration of War on Japan and Invasion of the Northeast

summary.zh: 苏联对日宣战并出兵中国东北，关东军迅速崩溃。
summary.en: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan and invaded Northeast China, rapidly collapsing the Kwantung Army.

description.zh:
1945 年 8 月 8 日（莫斯科时间），苏联对日宣战；8 月 9 日，苏军从东、北、西三个方向进入中国东北和朝鲜北部，进攻日本关东军。关东军在短时间内瓦解，日本投降进程明显加快。

本事件为国际事件，不绘制路线；日期按中国通行的 8 月 9 日标注，地点取东北方向示意点，待史料校订。
description.en:
The Soviet Union declared war on Japan on 8 August 1945 (Moscow time); on 9 August, Soviet forces entered Northeast China and northern Korea from the east, north, and west, attacking the Japanese Kwantung Army. The Kwantung Army collapsed quickly, significantly accelerating Japan’s surrender.

This is an international event with no route drawn; the date follows the conventional Chinese usage of 9 August, and the location is an illustrative point in the Northeast pending historical review.

summary.zh: 日本天皇广播《终战诏书》，宣布接受《波茨坦公告》，中国抗日战争取得胜利。
summary.en: The Japanese emperor broadcast the rescript accepting the Potsdam Declaration, bringing victory in China’s war of resistance.

description.zh:
1945 年 8 月 15 日，日本天皇裕仁通过广播发布《终战诏书》，宣布接受中美英苏四国发表的《波茨坦公告》，实际上宣布无条件投降。中国各地举行庆祝活动，抗日战争取得胜利。

本事件为政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与表述待史料校订。
description.en:
On 15 August 1945, Emperor Hirohito broadcast the Imperial Rescript on the Termination of the War, accepting the Potsdam Declaration issued by China, the United States, Britain, and the Soviet Union—in effect announcing unconditional surrender. Celebrations took place across China, marking victory in the war of resistance.

This is a political event with no route drawn; dates and wording await historical review.

name.en: Signing of the Japanese Instrument of Surrender

place.zh: 日本东京湾美国“密苏里”号战列舰

summary.zh: 日本代表在东京湾签署投降书，第二次世界大战正式结束。
summary.en: Japanese representatives signed the instrument of surrender in Tokyo Bay, formally ending the Second World War.

description.zh:
1945 年 9 月 2 日，日本政府代表在东京湾美国“密苏里”号战列舰上签署投降书，中、美、英、苏等同盟国代表签字接受。至此，中国抗日战争与第二次世界大战正式结束。

本事件为政治事件，不绘制路线；日期与地点为通行说法，待史料校订。
description.en:
On 2 September 1945, Japanese government representatives signed the instrument of surrender aboard the USS Missouri in Tokyo Bay, and representatives of the Allied powers, including China, the United States, Britain, and the Soviet Union, accepted it. China’s war of resistance and the Second World War formally ended.

This is a political event with no route drawn; date and location follow conventional accounts and await historical review.
